docs.title: mifarepy
docs.text: mifarepy is a Python library for interfacing with PROMAG RFID readers using the GNetPlus® serial protocol. It targets MIFARE Classic readers connected over RS-232/USB and exposes every documented command through a clean, typed Python API.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: Category What you get Card detection get_uid(), get_uid_int(), scan_tag(), is_card_present(), ping(), wait_for_card(), wait_for_card_async() Authentication authenticate_sector() (SAVE_KEY + AUTHENTICATE), authenticate_sector_cached() (AUTHENTICATE_KEY, skip reload) Block I/O read_block(), write_block(), read_sector(), write_sector(), write_sector_uniform() Bulk I/O read_blocks() / write_blocks() with per-sector SectorAuth Value blocks create_value_block(), read_value(), write_value(), increment_value(), decrement_value(), transfer(), restore() Reader control get_version(), set_auto_mode(), halt(), rf_power() Async wait_for_card_async() — non-blocking asyncio support Type safety @overload on read_block / get_second_sn, Literal['A','B'], SectorAuth, CardInfo Error detail InvalidMessage.raw_bytes, GNetPlusError.nak_code

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
from mifarepy import MifareReader

KEY = bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF')   # factory default

with MifareReader('/dev/ttyUSB0') as reader:
    print('Reader:', reader.get_version())
    print('Card UID:', reader.get_uid())         # e.g. '0xEDCEF8C3'

    reader.authenticate_sector(0, KEY)
    data = reader.read_sector(combine=True)      # 48-char hex string
    print('Sector 0 data:', data)

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for all public classes, dataclasses, exceptions, and methods in mifarepy v3.0.0.

docs.title: InvalidMessage
docs.text:
class InvalidMessage(Exception):
    raw_bytes: bytes  # partial bytes received before the error

Raised when a frame read from the serial port is malformed (wrong SOH, CRC mismatch, truncated data). raw_bytes holds whatever was read so you can inspect it during debugging.

docs.title: GNetPlusError
docs.text:
class GNetPlusError(Exception):
    raw: bytes               # raw NAK payload (typically 1 byte)
    code_description: str    # human-readable description from NAK code table
    nak_code: int            # integer value of raw[0], or 0 if multi-byte

Raised when the reader sends a NAK response.

NAK code table:

Code Meaning 0x01 Invalid address 0x02 Invalid message length 0x03 Invalid command 0x04 Card not present 0x05 Authentication failed 0x06 Block read failed 0x07 Block write failed 0x08 Value read failed 0x09 Value write failed 0x0A Access condition violation 0x0B Key not found 0x0C Timeout

docs.title: SectorAuth
docs.text:
@dataclass
class SectorAuth:
    key: bytes                        # 6-byte MIFARE authentication key (required)
    key_type: Literal['A', 'B'] = 'A'
    timeout: float = 1.0
    flush: bool = True

Per-sector authentication configuration used with the auth= parameter of read_blocks() / write_blocks(). Validates key_type and key length at construction time.

from mifarepy import SectorAuth

sa = SectorAuth(
    key=bytes.fromhex('A0A1A2A3A4A5'),
    key_type='B',
    timeout=2.0,
)

docs.title: CardInfo
docs.text:
@dataclass
class CardInfo:
    uid: str          # '0xAABBCCDD' (always 10 chars, upper-case)
    uid_int: int      # unsigned 32-bit integer
    uid_bytes: bytes  # raw 4-byte ANTI_COLLISION response (little-endian)

Returned by scan_tag().

card = reader.scan_tag()
str(card)         # '0xEDCEF8C3'
repr(card)        # "CardInfo(uid='0xEDCEF8C3')"
card.uid_int      # 3989956803
card.uid_bytes    # b'\xc3\xf8\xce\xed'

docs.title: Message / QueryMessage / ResponseMessage
docs.text:
Low-level GNetPlus® frame classes. You rarely need these directly.

Constant Opcode Description POLLING 0x00 Heartbeat / connectivity check GET_VERSION 0x01 Read firmware version string REQUEST 0x20 ISO 14443-3 REQUEST — wake IDLE cards ANTI_COLLISION 0x21 Get UID from a single card SELECT_CARD 0x22 Select a specific card by UID AUTHENTICATE 0x23 Authenticate a sector (after SAVE_KEY) READ_BLOCK 0x24 Read a 16-byte block WRITE_BLOCK 0x25 Write a 16-byte block READ_VALUE 0x27 Read a signed 32-bit value block CREATE_VALUE_BLOCK 0x28 Create/update a value block ACCESS_CONDITION 0x29 Set sector access conditions HALT 0x2A Put card into HALT state SAVE_KEY 0x2B Load authentication key into reader GET_SECOND_SN 0x2C Read 7-byte secondary UID GET_ACCESS_CONDITION 0x2D Read sector access conditions AUTHENTICATE_KEY 0x2E Authenticate using already-loaded key REQUEST_ALL 0x2F Wake ALL cards including HALT state RF_POWER_ONOFF 0x3E Toggle RF field power AUTO_MODE 0x3F Enable/disable EVN event notifications

docs.title: gencrc(msg_bytes)
docs.text:
def gencrc(msg_bytes: bytes) -> int: ...

Compute the 16-bit CRC checksum used by the GNetPlus® protocol.

docs.title: MifareReader
docs.text:
class MifareReader:
    port: str
    baudrate: int
    deviceaddr: int

Main entry point. All methods are synchronous unless noted.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
MifareReader(
    port: str = '/dev/ttyUSB0',
    baudrate: int = 19200,
    deviceaddr: int = 0,
    **kwargs,   # forwarded to serial.Serial
)

**kwargs is forwarded verbatim to serial.Serial, so you can pass timeout=, bytesize=, etc.

Raises RuntimeError if the port cannot be opened.

docs.title: Context manager / __repr__
docs.text:
with MifareReader('/dev/ttyUSB0') as reader:
    ...

repr(reader)
# "MifareReader(port='/dev/ttyUSB0', baudrate=19200, addr=0, open)"

close() disables auto mode before closing the port to avoid spurious EVN events in the next session.

docs.title: get_uid() -> str
docs.text:
Run REQUEST → ANTI_COLLISION and return the UID as '0xAABBCCDD'. Does not call SELECT — use scan_tag() when you need an active card.

uid = reader.get_uid()   # '0xEDCEF8C3'

docs.title: get_uid_int() -> int
docs.text:
Same as get_uid() but returns an unsigned 32-bit integer.

n = reader.get_uid_int()   # 3989956803

docs.title: get_sn(endian='little', as_string=True) (deprecated)
docs.text:
Deprecated in v3.0.0 Use get_uid() or get_uid_int() instead.

The endian parameter lets you choose byte order, which was confusing. The new methods always use little-endian (matching struct.pack('<L', ...)).

docs.title: request_all(endian='little', as_string=True) -> Union[str, int]
docs.text: REQUEST_ALL → ANTI_COLLISION — wakes cards that are in HALT state.

docs.title: get_second_sn(as_string=True) -> Union[str, bytes]
docs.text:
Read the 7-byte secondary UID (MIFARE Ultralight / DESFire).

@overload
def get_second_sn(self, as_string: Literal[True]) -> str: ...
@overload
def get_second_sn(self, as_string: Literal[False]) -> bytes: ...

docs.title: select_card() -> bytes
docs.text: REQUEST → ANTI_COLLISION → SELECT_CARD. Returns the ACK payload. Called automatically by authenticate_sector() — only call this directly for advanced multi-card workflows.

docs.title: scan_tag() -> CardInfo
docs.text:
One-shot: REQUEST → ANTI_COLLISION → SELECT_CARD. Returns a CardInfo dataclass. The card is left in the active state.

card = reader.scan_tag()
print(card)           # '0xEDCEF8C3'
print(card.uid_int)   # 3989956803

docs.title: ping() -> bool
docs.text:
Send POLLING (opcode 0x00) and return True if the reader acknowledges. Use this to verify the serial connection without interacting with any card.

if not reader.ping():
    raise RuntimeError('Reader not responding')

docs.title: is_card_present() -> bool
docs.text:
Non-blocking: send a single REQUEST and return True if a card responded. Does not select or authenticate the card.

while not reader.is_card_present():
    time.sleep(0.1)

docs.title: wait_for_card(timeout=10) -> Optional[str]
docs.text: Enable auto mode and block until a card arrives or timeout seconds elapse. Returns the card UID string. Raises TimeoutError.

docs.title: wait_for_card_async(timeout=10.0) -> str (async)
docs.text:
Non-blocking asyncio variant. Runs the blocking I/O in a thread-pool executor.

import asyncio

async def main():
    with MifareReader('/dev/ttyUSB0') as reader:
        uid = await reader.wait_for_card_async(timeout=15)
        print('Card:', uid)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: authenticate_sector(sector, key, key_type='A', timeout=1.0, flush=True)
docs.text:
Load a key into the reader (SAVE_KEY) and authenticate a sector (AUTHENTICATE).

  • Calls select_card() first — safe to call after any write operation.
  • key must be exactly 6 bytes.
  • key_type must be 'A' or 'B'.
reader.authenticate_sector(
    sector=1,
    key=bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF'),
    key_type='A',
)

docs.title: authenticate_sector_cached(sector, key_type='A', timeout=1.0)
docs.text:
Authenticate using the key that is already loaded in the reader (AUTHENTICATE_KEY, opcode 0x2E). Skips SAVE_KEY — faster for repeat-sector access with the same key.

Warning: The reader stores only one key at a time. If any other sector was authenticated between the last authenticate_sector call and this one, call authenticate_sector again.

docs.title: read_block(block, raw=False) -> Union[bytes, str]
docs.text:
Read a 16-byte block relative to the currently authenticated sector.

@overload
def read_block(self, block: int, raw: Literal[True]) -> bytes: ...
@overload
def read_block(self, block: int, raw: Literal[False] = ...) -> str: ...

block is relative to the sector (0–3; block 3 is the sector trailer).

docs.title: write_block(block, data) -> str
docs.text: Write exactly 16 bytes. data can be bytes or a 32-character hex string. Returns the reader's echoed ACK payload as a hex string.

docs.title: read_sector(sector=None, raw=False, combine=False)
docs.text:
Read blocks 0, 1, and 2 of the authenticated sector. Block 3 (trailer) is skipped.

  • combine=False (default) → {0: '...', 1: '...', 2: '...'}
  • combine=True, raw=False → single 96-char hex string
  • combine=True, raw=True → 48-byte bytes object

docs.title: write_sector(data)
docs.text:
Write data to blocks 0–2. Accepts:

  • 16 bytes (or 32-char hex) → same blob to all 3 blocks
  • 48 bytes (or 96-char hex) → split into three 16-byte chunks
  • dict mapping {0: ..., 1: ..., 2: ...} → write only specified blocks

docs.title: write_sector_uniform(data)
docs.text:
Explicit, intent-revealing alias for the 16-byte path of write_sector(). Writes the same 16 bytes to blocks 0, 1, and 2.

reader.write_sector_uniform(b'\x00' * 16)

docs.title: read_blocks(mapping, *, raw=False, combine=False, auth=None, keys=None, key_types='A', timeout=1.0, flush=True)
docs.text:
mapping: dict[int, list[int]]          # {sector: [block, block, ...]}
auth: Optional[dict[int, SectorAuth]]  # new-style per-sector auth
keys: ...                              # legacy — global or per-sector key bytes

Returns {sector: {block: data}}, or combined bytes/string when combine=True.

results = reader.read_blocks(
    {1: [0, 1, 2], 3: [0]},
    auth={
        1: SectorAuth(key=bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF')),
        3: SectorAuth(key=bytes.fromhex('A0A1A2A3A4A5'), key_type='B'),
    },
)

docs.title: write_blocks(mapping, *, auth=None, keys=None, key_types='A', timeout=1.0, flush=True)
docs.text:
mapping: dict[int, Union[bytes, str, dict[int, Union[str, bytes]]]]
auth: Optional[dict[int, SectorAuth]]

Same auth= / legacy style support as read_blocks.

docs.title: Value block operations
docs.text: Value blocks store a signed 32-bit integer in MIFARE redundant format. Authenticate the sector before any value block operation.

docs.title: create_value_block(block, initial_value=0)
docs.text: Initialize a block as a value block. Uses CREATE_VALUE_BLOCK (opcode 0x28).

docs.title: read_value(block) -> int
docs.text: Read a signed 32-bit value. Uses READ_VALUE (opcode 0x27).

docs.title: write_value(block, value)
docs.text: Write a signed 32-bit value. Delegates to create_value_block for compatibility with all firmware versions.

docs.title: increment_value(block, delta)
docs.text: Add delta (must be > 0) to the stored value. Read-modify-write. Raises ValueError on int32 overflow.

docs.title: decrement_value(block, delta)
docs.text: Subtract delta from the stored value. Raises ValueError on int32 underflow.

docs.title: transfer(source_block, dest_block)
docs.text: Copy value from source_block to dest_block within the same authenticated sector.

docs.title: restore(block)
docs.text: Re-read and re-write a block to ensure value block format integrity.

docs.title: get_version() -> str
docs.text:
Return the firmware/hardware version string.

reader.get_version()   # 'PGM0487 V1.4R0 (Build:110609)'

docs.title: set_auto_mode(enabled=True) -> bytes
docs.text: Enable (True) or disable (False) event-notification mode. When enabled, the reader spontaneously sends EVN frames on card arrival / departure.

docs.title: halt()
docs.text: Send HALT to put the current card into HALT state. The card will only respond to request_all() until it is removed and re-presented.

docs.title: rf_power(on: bool)
docs.text: Toggle the RF field. Power off + on resets cards that are in an inconsistent state.

docs.title: sendmsg(function, data=b'')
docs.text: Build and transmit a QueryMessage.

docs.title: readmsg(sink_events=False) -> ResponseMessage
docs.text: Read one ResponseMessage. If sink_events=True, EVN frames are silently discarded until a non-event frame arrives. Raises GNetPlusError on NAK.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
All example scripts live in the examples/ directory. They connect to a real reader on /dev/ttyUSB0 and use the factory-default key FFFFFFFFFFFF.

Before running any example, ensure the reader is plugged in and you have permission to access the serial port:

# Linux: add yourself to the dialout group
sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER   # re-login after this

examples/01_get_uid.py

Demonstrates get_uid(), get_uid_int(), and scan_tag().

python examples/01_get_uid.py

Calls get_version(), ping(), and prints repr(reader).

python examples/02_reader_info.py

docs.text:

Authenticates sector 1 and reads all three data blocks. Shows both dict and combined-string output modes.

python examples/03_read_sector.py

Writes a test pattern to sector 1 using write_sector(), then reads it back to verify.

python examples/04_write_sector.py

Uses read_blocks() with the new auth= / SectorAuth style to read blocks from multiple sectors in one call.

python examples/05_read_blocks.py

Shows create_value_block(), read_value(), increment_value(), decrement_value(), transfer(), and restore().

Demonstrates that authenticate_sector() safely re-selects the card after a write, avoiding the MIFARE IDLE-state NAK bug.

python examples/07_write_reauth.py

Uses wait_for_card_async() inside an asyncio.run() loop — ideal for non-blocking integration with FastAPI or Django async views.

docs.title: 📥 Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide covers different ways to install mifarepy and its prerequisites.

docs.title: ⚙️ Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python version: 3.7 or newer 🐍
  • pyserial: Installed automatically via PyPI, but ensure no conflicts.
  • Permissions (Linux): Add your user to the dialout group to access serial ports: 
    sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER
    Then log out and back in, or restart.
  • Windows: Identify your COM port (e.g., COM3) and install the driver if needed.

docs.title: 📦 Install from PyPI
docs.text:
The simplest way is via pip:

pip install mifarepy

This installs the latest stable release and its dependencies (including pyserial).

docs.title: 🔧 Editable / Development Install
docs.text:
If you plan to develop or contribute to mifarepy, install in editable mode:

git clone https://github.com/SparkDrago05/mifarepy.git
cd mifarepy
pip install -e .

This links the repository into your environment so changes are picked up immediately.

docs.title: 📁 Manual / Source Install
docs.text:
For environments without PyPI access, install from source:

git clone https://github.com/SparkDrago05/mifarepy.git
cd mifarepy
# Create a virtual environment (optional but recommended)
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate  # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

Note: Ensure requirements.txt is up to date. Alternatively, you can use pip install -e . as above.

docs.title: 🐍 Using pyproject.toml (PEP 517/518)
docs.text:
If you use modern tooling:

pip install build
python -m build  # will generate wheel and sdist in dist/
pip install dist/mifarepy-*.whl

docs.title: 🔍 Verify Installation
docs.text:
python -c "import mifarepy; print(mifarepy.__version__)"

You should see the installed version number, confirming a successful install.

For further configuration and advanced usage, see the API Reference and Usage Guide. 🎉

docs.title: Usage Guide
docs.text: This guide covers every major feature of mifarepy and is structured so you can read it top-to-bottom or jump directly to a section.

docs.title: Opening a connection
docs.text:
from mifarepy import MifareReader

# context manager (recommended — closes port automatically)
with MifareReader('/dev/ttyUSB0') as reader:
    ...

# explicit open / close
reader = MifareReader('/dev/ttyUSB0')
try:
    ...
finally:
    reader.close()

MifareReader accepts the same keyword arguments as serial.Serial (e.g. timeout=).

print(repr(reader))
# MifareReader(port='/dev/ttyUSB0', baudrate=19200, addr=0, open)

docs.title: Reader information
docs.text:
version = reader.get_version()
print(version)   # 'PGM0487 V1.4R0 (Build:110609)'

docs.title: One-shot UID
docs.text:
uid   = reader.get_uid()       # '0xEDCEF8C3'  (REQUEST + ANTI_COLLISION)
uid_i = reader.get_uid_int()   # 3989956803

get_sn() still works but emits a DeprecationWarning — migrate to get_uid().

docs.title: Quick check
docs.text:
if reader.is_card_present():
    print('card found')

docs.title: Full scan (REQUEST → ANTI_COLLISION → SELECT)
docs.text:
from mifarepy import CardInfo

card: CardInfo = reader.scan_tag()
print(card)           # '0xEDCEF8C3'
print(card.uid_int)   # 3989956803
print(card.uid_bytes) # b'\xc3\xf8\xce\xed'

docs.title: Wait for card (blocking / async)
docs.text:
uid = reader.wait_for_card(timeout=10)         # blocking

import asyncio
uid = asyncio.run(reader.wait_for_card_async(timeout=10))   # asyncio

docs.title: Heartbeat
docs.text: alive = reader.ping()   # True if reader responds to POLLING

docs.title: MIFARE Classic memory layout
docs.text:
MIFARE Classic 1K cards have 16 sectors × 4 blocks × 16 bytes = 1024 bytes.

Sector  Blocks (absolute)   Contents
  0       0, 1, 2, 3        Data (0-2) + Sector Trailer (3)
  1       4, 5, 6, 7        Data (0-2) + Sector Trailer (3)
  ...
 15      60,61,62,63        Data (0-2) + Sector Trailer (3)

The sector trailer (relative block 3) contains Key A, access bits, and Key B. mifarepy never writes block 3 through write_sector() or write_sector_uniform() — you must call write_block(3, ...) explicitly if you need to change keys.

docs.title: Standard (SAVE_KEY + AUTHENTICATE)
docs.text:
KEY_A = bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF')

reader.authenticate_sector(
    sector=1,
    key=KEY_A,
    key_type='A',    # 'A' or 'B'
    timeout=1.0,
    flush=True,
)

authenticate_sector automatically calls select_card() first, so it is safe to call immediately after any write operation.

docs.title: Cached (skip key reload)
docs.text:
# After authenticate_sector has already loaded a key once:
reader.authenticate_sector_cached(sector=2, key_type='A')

authenticate_sector_cached uses AUTHENTICATE_KEY (opcode 0x2E) and skips SAVE_KEY, saving ~50 ms per sector when the same key is reused.

docs.title: Single block
docs.text:
reader.authenticate_sector(sector=1, key=KEY_A)

# hex string (default)
hex_str: str   = reader.read_block(0)

# raw bytes
raw: bytes     = reader.read_block(0, raw=True)

# write (16 bytes or 32-char hex)
reader.write_block(0, b'\x00' * 16)
reader.write_block(0, '00' * 16)

docs.title: Sector-level
docs.text:
# read blocks 0, 1, 2 as a dict
result: dict = reader.read_sector(sector=1)
# {0: 'aabb...', 1: '...', 2: '...'}

# combine into single string
combined: str   = reader.read_sector(combine=True)
combined: bytes = reader.read_sector(raw=True, combine=True)  # 48 bytes

# write same data to all 3 data blocks
reader.write_sector(b'\x00' * 16)           # uniform — 16 bytes, repeated
reader.write_sector(b'\x00' * 48)           # split — 48 bytes → blocks 0/1/2
reader.write_sector({0: b'\xAA'*16, 2: b'\xBB'*16})   # selective dict

# explicit uniform helper (intent-revealing)
reader.write_sector_uniform(b'\x00' * 16)

docs.title: Bulk cross-sector I/O
docs.text:
from mifarepy import SectorAuth

# New-style with SectorAuth
results = reader.read_blocks(
    {1: [0, 1], 2: [0]},
    auth={
        1: SectorAuth(key=bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF')),
        2: SectorAuth(key=bytes.fromhex('A0A1A2A3A4A5'), key_type='B'),
    },
)

# Legacy-style (still supported)
results = reader.read_blocks(
    {1: [0, 1], 2: [0]},
    keys=bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF'),
    key_types='A',
)

# Write
reader.write_blocks(
    {1: {0: b'\xAA'*16, 1: b'\xBB'*16}, 2: {0: b'\xCC'*16}},
    auth={
        1: SectorAuth(key=bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF')),
        2: SectorAuth(key=bytes.fromhex('FFFFFFFFFFFF')),
    },
)

docs.title: Value blocks
docs.text:
Value blocks are a special MIFARE format that stores a signed 32-bit integer with built-in redundancy (stored three times: value, inverted value, value again).

reader.authenticate_sector(sector=2, key=KEY_A)

# Initialise
reader.create_value_block(block=0, initial_value=1000)

# Read
balance: int = reader.read_value(block=0)   # signed int

# Arithmetic
reader.increment_value(block=0, delta=50)
reader.decrement_value(block=0, delta=10)

# Overwrite
reader.write_value(block=0, value=9999)

# Copy between blocks (same sector)
reader.transfer(source_block=0, dest_block=1)

# Re-commit (repair after partial failure)
reader.restore(block=0)

docs.title: Reader control
docs.text:
# RF field power (useful for card reset without physical removal)
reader.rf_power(False)   # off
reader.rf_power(True)    # on

# Put card in HALT state (multi-card anti-collision)
reader.halt()

# Auto-mode: reader sends EVN events on card arrival/departure
reader.set_auto_mode(True)    # enable
reader.set_auto_mode(False)   # disable (called automatically by close())

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
from mifarepy import GNetPlusError, InvalidMessage

try:
    reader.authenticate_sector(0, KEY_A)
except GNetPlusError as e:
    print(e.code_description)   # 'Authentication failed'
    print(e.nak_code)           # 0x05
    print(repr(e.raw))          # b'\x05'

try:
    from mifarepy.protocol import Message
    msg = Message.readfrom(serial_port)
except InvalidMessage as e:
    print(e)                    # human error description
    print(e.raw_bytes.hex())    # partial bytes received before failure

docs.title: Type safety
docs.text:
from typing import reveal_type

# @overload: IDE knows exact return type
hex_str = reader.read_block(0, raw=False)   # str
raw     = reader.read_block(0, raw=True)    # bytes

# SectorAuth validates at construction time
from mifarepy import SectorAuth
SectorAuth(key=b'\xFF'*5)          # ValueError: key must be exactly 6 bytes
SectorAuth(key=b'\xFF'*6, key_type='C')  # ValueError: key_type must be 'A' or 'B'
